chunks.title: Lid anatomy refresher, hordeolum & chalazion
chunks.tldr: Lateral canthus sits 1–2 mm higher than medial. Upper lid: septum joins levator aponeurosis; preaponeurotic fat behind septum is the surgical landmark; levator inserts lower third of tarsus; crease low/absent in Asian lids. Hordeolum: acute staph infection — internal (meibomian) or external/stye (Zeis/Moll, points to skin). Warm compresses 10–15 min several times daily; I&D if not resolving in 48 h (vertical conjunctival or horizontal skin incision). Chalazion: sterile lipogranuloma from blocked meibomian gland (rosacea, posterior blepharitis); may cause astigmatism.
points: Chalazion: compresses → incision & curettage or intralesional steroid.
chunks.hook: Same chalazion again and again? Biopsy it.

cards.a: Granulomatous (lipogranulomatous) inflammation with Langhans-type giant cells.

chunks.title: Anterior & posterior blepharitis
chunks.tldr: Anterior: staphylococcal (dry scales, red ulcerated margins, lash loss; → hordeola, chalazia, inferior punctate keratitis, marginal keratitis) vs seborrhoeic (greasy scales, Malassezia, scalp/brow seborrhoea); often mixed. Rx: lid hygiene (baby shampoo scrub), antistaph ointment. Posterior (MGD): capped/inspissated glands, toothpaste secretions, telangiectatic rounded margins, frothy tears; linked to rosacea. Rx: warm compresses + expression; doxycycline 50–100 mg bd, azithromycin 1 g weekly ×3, topical metronidazole; brief weak steroid; preservative-free tears.
points: Both chronic, bilateral, may coexist; predispose to recurrent conjunctivitis.
Bacterial lipases disrupt the tear film.
chunks.hook: Dry scales = staph; greasy scales = seborrhoea; plugged glands = MGD.

cards.q: Systemic options for meibomian gland dysfunction?
cards.a: Oral doxycycline (50–100 mg bd) or azithromycin (1 g weekly for 3 weeks).

chunks.title: Entropion, trichiasis & ectropion
chunks.tldr: Entropion: involutional (commonest; lower lid; horizontal laxity + retractor disinsertion + overriding preseptal orbicularis), spastic, cicatricial (trachoma, OCP; upper or lower), congenital (don't confuse with epiblepharon — skin fold rolls lashes). Fix: lateral tightening, retractor repair, margin rotation; temporary tape/botox/Quickert sutures. Cicatricial: tarsal fracture/rotation, grafts. Trichiasis: epilate, electrolysis, laser, cryo. Distichiasis: extra lash row from meibomian orifices. Ectropion: involutional, paralytic (VII), cicatricial (skin graft), mechanical (remove mass), congenital → tearing, exposure.
points: Lid coloboma (upper medial) with limbal dermoid → Goldenhar; repair early if cornea at risk.

cards.q: Three components of involutional lower lid entropion?
cards.a: Horizontal lid laxity, lower lid retractor disinsertion, overriding preseptal orbicularis.

chunks.title: Epicanthus, telecanthus, chalasis & spasm
chunks.tldr: Epicanthus: vertical medial skin fold → pseudoesotropia; tarsalis (continuous with upper fold) vs inversus (into lower lid, blepharophimosis); fades by puberty. Telecanthus: intercanthal distance > palpebral fissure length (~30 mm); vs hypertelorism (wide orbits too, Crouzon). Blepharochalasis: young, recurrent painless lid oedema → thin 'crepe paper' skin, ptosis. Dermatochalasis: age-related excess skin; may block superior field → blepharoplasty. Benign essential blepharospasm: bilateral, women 3:1, basal ganglia circuit → botulinum toxin. Hemifacial spasm: unilateral, VII root compression by vessel → microvascular decompression or botox. Myokymia: benign lid twitch.
chunks.hook: Both eyes squeezing = blepharospasm; one side of face = hemifacial spasm.

cards.a: Vascular loop compressing the facial nerve root exit zone.

chunks.title: Ptosis classification
chunks.tldr: Upper lid normally sits midway between superior limbus and pupil. Congenital myogenic: dystrophic levator → poor excursion, lid lag on downgaze; 25% superior rectus weak. Blepharophimosis (FOXL2, AD; ptosis, telecanthus, epicanthus inversus; ovarian failure). Congenital neurogenic: III palsy, Horner (heterochromia; neuroblastoma), Marcus Gunn jaw-wink (V→levator synkinesis), CFEOM. Acquired aponeurotic (commonest; dehiscence, high crease, good excursion; trauma, surgery, contact lenses, pregnancy). Myogenic: CPEO/Kearns–Sayre, oculopharyngeal dystrophy (French-Canadian), myotonic dystrophy, myasthenia. Neurogenic: III palsy, Horner, botox. Mechanical: mass, oedema, scar. Pseudoptosis: dermatochalasis, contralateral retraction, hypotropia, enophthalmos.
points: MG: fatigue on upgaze, ice test, Cogan twitch; AChR antibodies 50–70% sensitive in ocular MG; single-fibre EMG 88–99%; screen for thymoma (~10%).
Horner: mild ptosis + lower lid elevation + miosis ± anhidrosis.
chunks.hook: High crease + good levator = aponeurotic; weak levator + lid lag = congenital.

chunks.title: Ptosis surgery
chunks.tldr: Choice depends on levator function. Good function: levator aponeurosis advancement/resection (skin approach) or Müller's muscle resection (conjunctival); ± superior tarsectomy. Poor function: frontalis sling (autologous/allogeneic fascia lata, silicone, Mersilene, Gore-Tex). Caution if poor closure or absent Bell's phenomenon (exposure). Symmetry in all gazes only if levator works. Children: watch for deprivation amblyopia, astigmatism, strabismus; observe mild ptosis until 4–5 yr; operate early if amblyopia or chin-up posture. MG: treat medically first.

cards.q: Indication for early ptosis surgery in a child?
cards.a: Amblyopia (visual axis occlusion/astigmatism) or worsening chin-up head posture.

chunks.title: Benign lid tumours
chunks.tldr: Squamous papilloma (skin tag). Seborrhoeic keratosis (stuck-on, warty, older adults). Keratoacanthoma: rapid crater with keratin plug, involutes in ~6 months; SCC variant? — excise; multiple → Muir–Torre (colorectal cancer). Actinic keratosis: scaly; up to 20% → SCC. Naevi: junctional → compound → intradermal (often amelanotic in adults). Adnexal: sebaceous adenoma, trichoepithelioma. Capillary haemangioma: appears weeks after birth, grows ~1 yr, involutes (30% by 3, 70–90% by 7) → treat for amblyopia, optic neuropathy, exposure with propranolol (monitor: bradycardia, hypoglycaemia, bronchospasm) or topical timolol. Port-wine stain (Sturge–Weber). Lymphangioma: bleeds after trauma/URTI. Choristomas: dermoid (lateral brow).
chunks.hook: Strawberry baby lid → propranolol if it threatens vision.

cards.q: First-line systemic treatment for vision-threatening periocular capillary haemangioma?

chunks.title: Malignant lid tumours
chunks.tldr: BCC (~90%): from pluripotent basal stem cells; lower lid 65%; pearly nodule, rolled edge, telangiectasia, lash loss; local invasion. Rx: biopsy → excision with margin control or Mohs; vismodegib (hedgehog inhibitor) for advanced. SCC (5–10%): hyperkeratotic → ulcerates; lymph node spread, perineural invasion. Sebaceous carcinoma: tarsal nodule/diffuse thickening, lash loss, masquerades as recurrent chalazion/blepharitis; pagetoid spread; oil red O; map biopsies; wide excision; Muir–Torre. Melanoma (1%): check preauricular/submandibular nodes. Lymphoma: lids often T-cell (mycosis fungoides). Kaposi (HHV-8, AIDS). Metastases: poor survival.
points: Risks: UV, radiation, fair skin, >50, immunosuppression, arsenic, xeroderma pigmentosum.

cards.a: Intraepithelial spread of tumour cells (e.g. sebaceous carcinoma) into conjunctival/skin epithelium away from the main mass.

chunks.title: Tear film & secretory disorders
chunks.tldr: Tear film: mucin (goblet cells) / aqueous (lacrimal + Krause/Wolfring) / lipid (meibomian). Reflex arc: V1 afferent → superior salivary nucleus → nervus intermedius → greater petrosal → Vidian nerve → pterygopalatine ganglion → zygomatic → lacrimal nerve. Alacrima: Riley–Day, anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, CPA surgery. Hypersecretion: mostly reflex from surface disease. Crocodile tears (aberrant VII after Bell's) → botox to gland. Dacryoadenitis: acute (children, viral — mumps, EBV; S-shaped lid) vs chronic >1 month (sarcoid, Graves, Sjögren, SLE, IgG4; lymphoma mimic → biopsy).

cards.a: Aberrant regeneration of the facial nerve after Bell's palsy (salivary fibres reach the lacrimal gland).

chunks.title: NLDO, dacryocystitis & canaliculitis
chunks.tldr: Pump: blink tightens orbicularis around ampulla → canaliculi shorten → negative pressure in sac. Congenital NLDO: imperforate valve of Hasner; up to 8% of newborns, 90% open by 1 month; massage; probe if >6 months or acute dacryocystitis (75% success once), then repeat probe, turbinate infracture, silicone tubes, balloon; never probe during acute infection. Adult NLDO: postmenopausal women → DCR (external or endonasal). Acute dacryocystitis: painful swelling below medial canthal tendon → systemic antibiotics (orbital cellulitis risk). Do DCR before elective intraocular surgery. Canaliculitis: Actinomyces, pouting punctum, sulphur granules → curettage/canaliculotomy.
points: Canalicular stenosis: viral (zoster, HSV, adeno), SJS, OCP, 5-FU, idoxuridine → stent or CDCR with Jones tube.
chunks.hook: Infected sac → no cataract surgery until DCR.

cards.q: When is probing indicated for congenital NLDO (per Vaughan)?
cards.a: Persistent stenosis beyond 6 months or an episode of acute dacryocystitis (not during active infection).
